text: Cirrus clouds form delicate filaments high in the atmosphere. Their substance is ice, even when the sky below is warm.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Cirrocumulus appears as small bright grains or ripples high in the sky, usually without the dark shading of larger cloud heaps.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Cirrostratus can spread a thin veil over the sky. Ice crystals in the veil often produce a halo around the Sun or Moon.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Altocumulus forms midlevel patches or layers of rounded cloud elements, sometimes arranged into rolls.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Altostratus is a gray or blue-gray sheet through which the Sun can look like light seen through frosted glass.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Nimbostratus forms a thick, dark layer associated with continuing rain or snow. Ragged lower clouds may gather underneath it.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Cumulus has distinct boundaries, growing into sunlit mounds above a darker, roughly level base.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Cumulonimbus is the towering cloud of a thunderstorm; its upper region often spreads into an anvil.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Stratocumulus spreads in low patches or layers of rounded masses, with darker gaps and shading between the elements.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Stratus makes a low, comparatively uniform cloud sheet. It can produce drizzle or small snow grains.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, Ten Basic Clouds; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/ten-basic-clouds. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A hailstone grows as supercooled liquid droplets collide with it and freeze onto its surface inside a thunderstorm.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Rapid freezing traps air bubbles and makes cloudy ice; slower freezing lets bubbles escape and makes clearer ice. A layered hailstone records changing conditions.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Hail falls when an updraft can no longer support it, either because the stone has grown or because the updraft has weakened.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Strong winds can drive falling hail at an angle, even nearly sideways.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Alternating clear and cloudy layers in hail do not simply count trips up and down through a storm. Temperature, liquid-water content, and horizontal motion matter.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A supercell contains a persistent rotating updraft. Its organized internal motion can allow the storm to last for hours.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Thunderstorm FAQ; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/thunderstorms/faq/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Condensing water vapor releases heat. That release supplies a substantial part of a thunderstorm's energy.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Thunderstorm FAQ; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/thunderstorms/faq/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A derecho is a widespread, long-lived windstorm associated with a fast-moving band of showers or thunderstorms. Its damage often follows a relatively straight swath.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Thunderstorm FAQ; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/thunderstorms/faq/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Hail can form high in a thunderstorm and then melt before it reaches the ground.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Thunderstorm FAQ; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/thunderstorms/faq/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Wind flowing past a tall island can leave a wake of alternating rotating eddies. Clouds make the otherwise invisible vortex street visible from above.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA JetStream, NASA satellite observations of Canary Island cloud vortices; https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream. Consulted 2026-10-13.
